sections.heading: 1. Purpose
sections.body: This template structures an assessment of the potential impacts of an AI system on individuals, groups and society, which is central to the responsible-AI approach of ISO/IEC 42001.

sections.heading: 2. Scope
sections.body: A single AI system; complete one assessment per system or significant change.

sections.heading: 3. Conducting the Assessment
sections.body: Complete the sections below for the AI system, proportionate to its risk.

rows: [FILL IN: the AI system and its intended purpose]
Individuals, groups and society potentially affected
Benefits and harms, including fairness, safety, privacy, autonomy and environmental impacts
Assessment of how likely and how serious each impact is
Measures to prevent or reduce harms, including human oversight
The remaining impact and the decision to proceed, change or stop

sections.heading: 4. When and How Often
sections.body: An assessment is carried out before deploying a new AI system or making a significant change to an existing one, is proportionate to the system's risk, draws on diverse input where appropriate, and is reviewed periodically and when the system or its context changes.

sections.heading: 5. Disclaimer
sections.body: This template is an independently created resource to help you implement a management system aligned to the relevant ISO standard. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or certified by ISO or any standards body, does not reproduce the text of the standard, and is not a substitute for professional advice or certification by an accredited body. Obtain the official standard from ISO.

sections.heading: 7. Testing & Maintenance
sections.body: This plan is reviewed at least annually and after every activation or major change. Exercises (tabletop or full) are scheduled to validate the plan and results are recorded as improvement actions.

sections.heading: 1. Purpose
sections.body: This AI policy sets the organisation's intentions and principles for the responsible development and use of AI, providing the framework for AI objectives, consistent with the approach of ISO/IEC 42001.

sections.heading: 2. Scope
sections.body: All AI systems the organisation develops, provides, deploys or uses.

sections.heading: 3. Principles
sections.body:
The organisation commits to managing AI responsibly:
- AI is used for legitimate purposes and in line with the organisation's values and obligations.
- AI risks, including risks to individuals, groups and society, are assessed and managed.
- AI systems are developed and used with appropriate transparency, oversight and accountability.
- Data used for AI is handled responsibly and lawfully.

sections.heading: 4. Objectives and Governance
sections.body: AI objectives are set and reviewed, roles are assigned, and the AI management system is resourced, monitored and improved. [FILL IN: reference your AI objectives.]

sections.heading: 5. Disclaimer
sections.body: This template is an independently created resource to help you implement a management system aligned to the relevant ISO standard. It is not affiliated with, endorsed by, or certified by ISO or any standards body, does not reproduce the text of the standard, and is not a substitute for professional advice or certification by an accredited body. Obtain the official standard from ISO.

rows: Owns the policy, approves exceptions, monitors compliance and reports to leadership.

sections.heading: 7. Compliance & Enforcement
sections.body: Compliance with this policy is mandatory. Violations may result in disciplinary action up to and including termination of employment or contract, and may be reported to relevant authorities where required by law.

sections.heading: 8. Exceptions
sections.body: Any exception to this policy must be requested in writing, risk-assessed, and approved by [Approver / CISO] at [Company Name]. Approved exceptions are documented, time-bound and reviewed at expiry.

sections.heading: 9. Review
sections.body: This policy is reviewed at least annually, or after a significant change or security incident, and updated as required.

sections.heading: 1. Purpose
sections.body: This document assigns the roles and responsibilities for the AI management system and for the AI systems within its scope, consistent with the approach of ISO/IEC 42001.

sections.heading: 2. Scope
sections.body: The people and functions involved in governing, developing, deploying and using AI systems.

sections.heading: 3. Roles
sections.body:
Responsibility and authority for AI are assigned across the lifecycle:
- Roles cover AI governance, risk management, data, development, deployment, human oversight and incident handling.
- Top management retains accountability for the AIMS and provides the resources for it.
- Where AI decisions can affect individuals, the role responsible for human oversight is named.
- [FILL IN: list your AI roles and who holds them.]

sections.heading: 4. Responsibilities
sections.body:
Each role's responsibilities are defined so AI systems are managed end to end:
- Responsibilities for the AIMS and for each stage of the AI lifecycle are assigned to named roles.
- The people assigned have, or are given, the necessary competence for their AI responsibilities.
- Escalation routes are defined for AI risks, incidents and oversight interventions.

sections.heading: 1. Purpose
sections.body: This policy governs the AI system lifecycle, from objectives and design through development, verification, deployment, operation and retirement, consistent with the approach of ISO/IEC 42001.

sections.heading: 2. Scope
sections.body: All AI systems the organisation develops or significantly configures.

sections.heading: 3. Lifecycle Stages
sections.body:
AI systems are managed through defined stages:
- Objectives and requirements, including intended purpose and acceptance criteria.
- Design and development, with responsible-AI considerations built in.
- Verification and validation, including testing for performance and for risks such as bias.
- Deployment and operation, with monitoring and human oversight.
- Retirement and decommissioning.

sections.heading: 4. Documentation and Change
sections.body: Each AI system is documented, and changes are controlled and re-assessed for impact and risk.

sections.heading: 1. Purpose
sections.body: This policy covers providing information to interested parties about AI systems and governing their responsible use, consistent with the approach of ISO/IEC 42001.

sections.heading: 2. Scope
sections.body: AI systems that interact with or affect users, customers or other interested parties.

sections.heading: 3. Information to Interested Parties
sections.body:
People who use or are affected by an AI system are given what they need to understand it:
- Its purpose, and where appropriate that they are interacting with or affected by AI.
- Its capabilities and limitations, in terms the audience can understand.
- How to raise a question, concern or complaint about it.
- [FILL IN: list your AI touchpoints and the information provided at each.]

sections.heading: 4. Responsible Use
sections.body:
Use is kept within intended bounds:
- The intended use of each AI system is defined, and uses outside it are discouraged or prevented.
- Feedback and concerns are captured and acted on.

sections.heading: 1. Purpose
sections.body: This document defines the scope of the organisation's AI management system (AIMS), the boundary of what is managed under it, consistent with the approach of ISO/IEC 42001.

sections.heading: 2. Scope
sections.body: The AI systems, processes, people and locations included in the AI management system.

sections.heading: 3. Context
sections.body:
The organisation establishes the context for managing its AI systems:
- The internal and external issues relevant to its AI objectives are considered.
- The interested parties (regulators, customers, affected individuals, internal stakeholders) and their requirements are identified.
- The legal, regulatory and ethical obligations that apply to its AI use are recorded.
- [FILL IN: summarise your context, interested parties and obligations.]

sections.heading: 4. Scope
sections.body:
The AIMS scope is defined explicitly:
- It covers the AI systems, activities and organisational units that are managed under the system.
- The interfaces and dependencies at the boundary (including third-party AI components and services) are stated.
- Any exclusions are stated with a justification.
- [FILL IN: define the scope, the systems and units included, and any exclusions.]

sections.heading: 5. Roles in the AI Lifecycle
sections.body: The roles the organisation plays, for example as a provider, deployer or user of AI systems, are stated, because they determine which obligations and controls apply across the AI lifecycle.

sections.heading: 1. Purpose
sections.body: This policy governs the data used to develop and operate AI systems, so it is appropriate, well-understood and responsibly handled, consistent with the approach of ISO/IEC 42001.

sections.heading: 2. Scope
sections.body: The data used to train, test and operate the organisation's AI systems.

sections.heading: 3. Data Quality and Provenance
sections.body:
Data feeding AI systems is fit for purpose and understood:
- Data is selected for relevance and quality for the intended use.
- Its provenance (where it came from and how) and any limitations are documented.
- [FILL IN: describe your data sources and quality checks.]

sections.heading: 4. Responsible Use
sections.body:
Data is handled lawfully and fairly:
- Data is used lawfully and for legitimate purposes, with privacy and other obligations met.
- Bias and representativeness are considered and addressed where they could cause harm.

sections.heading: 5. Management
sections.body: Data used by AI systems is documented, access-controlled and retained appropriately.
